implementation: Allow PENDING -> FAILED in the core transfer lifecycle; existing atomic controller validation still enforces all attempt/assignment/job references, CAS, lease, progress, outcome, fencing and sequence invariants.
Track acknowledgement of IN_PROGRESS in each agent execution and explicitly pass ACCEPTED or IN_PROGRESS as the FAILED report's expected state.
Replay attempt-aware transient reports unchanged, at most three sends with 100/200ms delays and a per-send response deadline; do not replay legacy non-attempt reports or definitive 4xx rejections.
Distinguish a rejected/unresolved status acknowledgement from an execution failure and do not manufacture a later report or execute after an unacknowledged start.

Suppress repeated local claims for one job/attempt/fencing generation until lease expiry. Build the executable request before start acknowledgement; governed final path validation stays on a worker and closes credentials on preparation failure.
limitations: Agent boundary tests use real HTTP against a controlled protocol fixture; complementary controller tests use the real HTTP handler and Raft application in explicit volatile node mode. The snapshot assertion is a codec round trip, not a WAL/disk restart. No internal storage backend is introduced. This is not a single agent-to-production-controller cross-module deployment test.

Exact-payload bounded replay reconciles transient lost acknowledgements. Prolonged outages, durable agent report-outbox recovery, automatic lease expiry/reassignment and destination reconciliation remain Phase 2 work; operator guidance is in deployment guide section 12.
No deployed data was changed. R1 production durability and R6 final release gates remain open; this record does not close Phase 2 or Phase 4 overall.
